arxiv-2304-03037.title: Parallel circuit implementation of variational quantum algorithms
arxiv-2304-03037.creator: Michele Cattelan, Sheir Yarkoni
arxiv-2304-03037.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Michele Cattelan, Sheir Yarkoni. We present a method to split quantum circuits of variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) to allow for parallel training and execution, that maximally exploits the limited number of qubits in hardware to solve large problem instances. We apply this specifically to combinatorial optimization problems, where inherent structures from the problem can be identified, thus directly informing how to create these parallelized quantum circuits, which we call slices.

arxiv-2304-09383.title: Denoising Diffusion Medical Models
arxiv-2304-09383.creator: Pham Ngoc Huy, and Tran Minh Quan Email : {hpham, qtran}@talosix.com
arxiv-2304-09383.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Pham Ngoc Huy, and Tran Minh Quan Email : {hpham, qtran}@talosix.com. In this study, we introduce a generative model that can synthesize a large number of radiographical image/label pairs, and thus is asymptotically favorable to downstream activities such as segmentation in bio-medical image analysis. Denoising Diffusion Medical Model (DDMM), the proposed technique, can create realistic X-ray images and associated segmentations on a small number of annotated datasets as well as other massive unlabeled datasets with no supervision.

arxiv-2404-19657.title: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of the Tunneling Potential
arxiv-2404-19657.creator: José R. Espinosa
arxiv-2404-19657.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by José R. Espinosa. The Tunneling Potential Formalism was introduced to calculate the tunneling actions that control vacuum decay as an alternative to the standard Euclidean Formalism. The new approach sets the problem as a simple variational problem in field space with decay described by a tunneling potential function V t V_{t} that extremizes a simple action functional S ⁡ [ V t ] S[V_{t}] and has a number of appealing properties that have been presented elsewhere.

arxiv-2505-18584.title: Unleashing Diffusion Transformers for Visual Correspondence by Modulating Massive Activations
arxiv-2505-18584.creator: Chaofan Gan Yuanpeng Tu Xi Chen Tieyuan Chen, Yuxi Li Mehrtash Harandi Weiyao Lin
arxiv-2505-18584.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Chaofan Gan Yuanpeng Tu Xi Chen Tieyuan Chen, Yuxi Li Mehrtash Harandi Weiyao Lin. Pre-trained stable diffusion models (SD) have shown great advances in visual correspondence. In this paper, we investigate the capabilities of Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) for accurate dense correspondence. Distinct from SD, DiTs exhibit a critical phenomenon in which very few feature activations exhibit significantly larger values than others, known as massive activations , leading to uninformative representations and significant performance degradation for DiTs.

arxiv-2509-04541.description: Abstract Deep Learning is evolving fast and integrates into various domains. Finance is a challenging field for deep learning, especially in the case of interpretable artificial intelligence (AI). Although classical approaches perform very well with natural language processing, computer vision, and forecasting, they are not perfect for the financial world, in which specialists use different metrics to evaluate model performance.

arxiv-2601-14925.creator: Nicolás Arrieta Larraza, Niels de Koeijer
arxiv-2601-14925.description: Abstract Single-channel speech enhancement algorithms are often used in resource-constrained embedded devices, where low latency and low complexity designs gain more importance. In particular, a recent deep learning model named ULCNet is among the state-of-the-art approaches in this domain.

pmc-12786755.title: Concordance Analysis Between Sputum and Bronchoscopic Specimens on Nontuberculous Mycobacteria Pulmonary Disease
pmc-12786755.creator: Sojung Park, Jin Hwa Lee, Nam Eun Kim, Yune-Young Shin
pmc-12786755.description: Background/Objectives: This study evaluated the concordance between sputum and bronchoscopic specimens in diagnosing nontuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) pulmonary disease. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed patients with NTM isolated from respiratory specimens between 2010 and 2022. Our analysis assessed species concordance across the two diagnostic methods and compared clinical outcomes between patients with multiple positive cultures and those with a single positive culture.

pmc-12950039.title: Motion sensations, postural sway, and side effects for copolar galvanic vestibular stimulation
pmc-12950039.creator: Caroline R Austin, Luc Willett, Torin K Clark
pmc-12950039.description: Galvanic vestibular stimulation (GVS), traditionally applied with oppositely polarized electrodes on the two mastoids (behind the ears), produces self-tilt/rotation perceptions and postural reflexes primarily about the head-centered roll axis (i.e., out the nose). However, there are reports of non-vestibular side effects, such as skin tingling at the electrodes, metallic taste, and visual flashes, which have not been systematically characterized.

pmc-13356636.title: Pulmonary embolism after treatment for massive hemoptysis: a therapeutic dilemma
pmc-13356636.creator: Toshiyuki Yonezawa, Akiko Narita, Kojiro Suzuki, Naoki Ozeki, Takayuki Fukui, Satoru Ito
pmc-13356636.description: Massive hemoptysis is a life-threatening condition requiring prompt hemostatic intervention. After hemostatic treatment, thromboembolic complications may pose a dilemma when anticoagulation is necessary but carries a risk of rebleeding. A 72-year-old man with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease was admitted for recurrent hemoptysis. Bronchial angiography revealed a markedly dilated right bronchial artery with intrapulmonary shunting.

pmc-13495287.title: Parental hesitancy and refusal toward routine childhood vaccination after the COVID-19 vaccination period: a cross-sectional study
pmc-13495287.creator: Ozan Emre Eliaçık, Oğulcan Çöme, Tolga Günvar
pmc-13495287.description: BackgroundThe COVID-19 pandemic intensified public debates on vaccines, amplifying concerns about safety, side effects, rapid development, and institutional trust. These concerns may be associated with current attitudes toward routine childhood immunization. This study assessed parental intentions regarding routine childhood vaccination among parents whose children had previously completed routine immunizations.

pmc-13536298.title: Accuracy of digital impressions captured by an intraoral scanner in a partially edentulous mandible

pmc-13536298.description: Background/purposeThe effectiveness of intraoral scanners in accurately recording partially edentulous mandibles is still under scrutiny. This study aimed to assess the accuracy of digital impressions obtained using an intraoral scanner in a partially edentulous mandibular arch.Materials and methodsA partially edentulous typodont model with missing five teeth was digitally scanned using a calibrated desktop scanner to create a reference model.

pmc-13676512.title: Central Nervous System Reservoirs and HIV Cure: Therapeutic Opportunities and Challenges
pmc-13676512.creator: Thomas A Angelovich, Michael Roche, Paul R Gorry, Melissa J Churchill
pmc-13676512.description: Purpose of reviewDespite viral suppression with antiretroviral therapy, people with HIV (PWH) remain at increased risk of neurocognitive impairment, neuroinflammation, and potential viral rebound following therapy interruption. Although the central nervous system (CNS) is a recognised HIV reservoir, it is often not fully considered in cure approaches.

uslaw-usc-t18-s1072.title: 18 U.S.C. § 1072 — Concealing escaped prisoner
uslaw-usc-t18-s1072.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t18-s1072.description: United States Code, Title 18 (Crimes And Criminal Procedure); Part I (Crimes); Chapter 49 (Fugitives From Justice). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Whoever willfully harbors or conceals any prisoner after his escape from the custody of the Attorney General or from a Federal penal or correctional institution, shall be imprisoned not more than three years.
